newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE COUNT ON MERLE TO RESTORE PRIDE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE COUNT ON MERLE TO RESTORE PRIDE.

text.p: France hope powerful lock Oliver Merle, back in a revamped team for the second test against rugby union world champions South Africa in Paris on Saturday, will help them restore some pride.

"Olivier has always been a first choice player this season and we missed him a lot last Saturday," said French coach Jean-Claude Skrela, referring to the first test won 22-12 by the Springboks in Bordeaux.
Merle, fit again after a rib injury, is a tough customer in lineouts, scrums and mauls and is the sort of player France need to challenge the strong Springbok forwards.

Skrela, who has had to cope with a string of injuries, on Wednesday unveiled a team with six new names including Bourgoin winger Laurent Leflamand, who will earn his first cap, and two changes of position.
"I'm very proud," said Leflamand, 28. "From what I saw last week, we will have to watch (Springbok fullback Andre) Joubert carefully because he did us a lot of harm."
The other players to come in are winger David Venditti, flyhalf Christophe Lamaison, scrumhalf Guy Accoceberry and hooker Marc Dal Maso.
Richard Dourthe switches from wing to centre while captain Abdelatif Benazzi moves from flanker to number eight.

"The players must understand that if you want to run the ball, you have to fight to win it first," said Skrela. "We thought that was obvious at international level but it didn't look that way in the first test."

For the first time in their history, the Springboks will play four successive tests with the same team as their squad for Saturday's match is unchanged from the one who won the first test and two previous tests against the Pumas in Argentina.
Hooker James Dalton, who left the pitch in Bordeaux with a bruised shoulder, should be fit to play and so should Joubert despite a minor thigh injury sustained while training this week.

France - 15-Jean-Luc Sadourny; 14-Laurent Leflamand, 13-Richard Dourthe, 12-Stephane Glas, 11-David Venditti; 10-Christophe Lamaison, 9-Guy Accoceberry; 8-Abdelatif Benazzi (cap), 7-Richard Castel, 6-Philippe Benetton, 5-Fabien Pelous, 4-Olivier Merle, 3-Franck Tournaire, 2-Marc Dal Maso, 1-Christian Califano.

South Africa - 15-Andre Joubert; 14-James Small, 13-Japie Mulder, 12-Hennie Le Roux, 11-Jacques Olivier; 10-Henry Honiball, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen; 8-Gary Teichmann (captain), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Ruben Kruger, 5-Mark Andrews, 4-Kobus Wiese, 3-Adrian Garvey, 2-James Dalton, 1-Dawie Theron.
